summary.intent: Plan Phase 21 (BYO-IPFS Node Support), run a pre-implementation security review of the planning docs, and document benchmarking tasks as an additional plan in the phase.
summary.outcome: Phase 21 was planned with 6 plans across 4 waves (passing verification on iteration 2/3), a security review identified 1 critical + 2 high issues in the planning docs, and a 7th benchmarking plan (21-07-PLAN.md) was added to the phase covering baseline capture and mixed-load scenarios with provider selection deferred.

repo: Current IPFS upload pipeline makes 3 Kubo pin calls per upload (~1.37s each), accounting for ~95% of upload endpoint time; staging VPS plateaus at 23-28 ops/s and errors at 200 concurrent clients.
BYO+Kubo external-only mode reduces per-upload API time from ~4.2s to ~105ms (40x), shifting the bottleneck from Kubo pin throughput to PostgreSQL write throughput.
BYO+PSA external-only still routes ciphertext through CipherBox as a transient relay before PSA pinByCid, so it does NOT free up Kubo capacity — nearly identical load profile to non-BYO users.
Existing load test harness is in tests/load/src/scenarios/ with client-pool abstraction; upload-throughput.test.ts is the reference scenario for new BYO scenarios.
Baselines from Phase 19.2 post-optimization are the current reference point for performance comparisons.
TEE republish route correctly uses Uint8Array.fill(0) for IPNS key cleanup — this pattern must be followed in the new migration worker.
Plan frontmatter uses indented list format for requirements (two spaces + dash) which caused a grep to miss BYO-06 when checking coverage with a simple grep.

code.finding: TEE migration worker fetchFromProvider/pinToProvider accept arbitrary user-provided URLs after ECIES decryption with no SSRF protection — must add HTTPS enforcement, private IP blocking, and DNS rebinding protection before implementation.
POST /ipfs/register-cid endpoint has no CID format validation, no size cap, and no check that the caller is actually a BYO user — non-BYO users could exploit to bypass quota enforcement.
Migration worker decrypts auth tokens as JSON strings which are immutable in JS and cannot be zeroed — credentials must be kept as Uint8Array throughout to enable proper memory cleanup.
Correct pattern for TEE key cleanup: Uint8Array.fill(0) — reference implementation for migration worker to follow.

workflow: Plan checker caught 5 blockers on the first pass — the revision loop (plan-phase step 12) is doing real work, not just rubber-stamping.
Security review on planning docs (pre-implementation) is more effective than post-implementation review; SSRF and authorization gaps are easier to fix in the plan than in code.
markdownlint rejects bold-as-heading patterns (**Assessment: ...**) in markdown files, causing commit hook failures — use plain text or proper heading syntax instead.
Separating capacity benchmarks (can use mock with realistic latency) from integration benchmarks (needs real provider) prevents over-engineering test infrastructure.
Background agents (security review) can run concurrently with other discussions without blocking the main thread — useful for parallelizing slow analysis tasks.

friction: markdownlint pre-commit hook rejected the security review report due to bold-as-heading patterns, requiring multiple sequential Edit calls to fix each instance before the commit succeeded.
Plan frontmatter requirement IDs use indented list format that a simple grep missed, causing a false negative in the requirements coverage gate that needed manual follow-up verification.

Plan checker identified 5 blockers on the first pass, requiring a full revision loop iteration — the locked decision violations (no server relay, fail with clear error) should have been caught by the planner originally.
open_items: Security: SSRF protection in TEE migration worker (Plan 05 Task 2) — must add HTTPS enforcement, private IP blocklist, and DNS rebinding protection before implementing migration-worker.ts.
Security: CID registration authorization gate (Plan 02 Task 1) — add BYO user check, CID format validation (CIDv1 base32), and size cap to POST /ipfs/register-cid.
Security: TEE migration worker credential handling — process decrypted auth tokens as Uint8Array throughout to enable zeroing after use.
Benchmarking: External IPFS provider selection for load tests is deferred — Pinata rate limits on paid vs test account need evaluation; Filebase noted as alternative.
Benchmarking: CI strategy for BYO load tests requiring an external Kubo node is unresolved — second Kubo instance, container, or controlled mock TBD.
Benchmarking: Mixed-load ratio sweep (CB-only + BYO users) and PSA transient relay path under concurrent load are new test scenarios to implement in Phase 21 Wave 4 (Plan 07).
25+ security test cases in the review report need to be translated into actual test files — not yet assigned to any plan or wave.
